exchange.summary: LDAP search base=DC=scaffold,DC=htb scope=sub filter=(objectClass=*) attrs=[objectClass,cn,sAMAccountName,… +49]
273 entries returned

findings.impact: Any compromised principal in the listed path can write the ACL, gain DCSync/GenericAll on Tier-0, extract the krbtgt hash, and forge a golden ticket. Cost=1 means one dangerous action away, not one hop of pivoting.
findings.remediation: Review the listed principals and remove unexpected ACEs (WriteDacl/GenericAll/Replication rights); re-apply the AdminSDHolder template where appropriate.

findings.impact: Attacker enrolls a v1 template requesting Client-Auth in the application policies, receives a cert usable for PKINIT, gets a TGT as any target account (SAN-supplied). CVE-2024-49019 exploitation.
findings.remediation: Upgrade v1 templates to v2+, require manager approval, or restrict enrollment; apply the CVE-2024-49019 patch.

exchange.summary: LDAP search base=DC=scaffold,DC=htb scope=sub filter=(objectClass=*) attrs=[objectClass,cn,sAMAccountName,… +49]
273 entries returned

findings.impact: Attacker writes msDS-KeyCredentialLink on the Tier-0 target, then PKINITs with the freshly-generated cert to obtain a TGT as that principal. Full impersonation of a Domain Admin without ever learning their password.
findings.remediation: Remove unexpected WriteProperty on msDS-KeyCredentialLink and audit AdminSDHolder inheritance on privileged accounts.

findings.title: Populated sensitive / Tier-0-equivalent groups
findings.detail: Members of Account/Backup/Print/Server Operators and DnsAdmins can escalate to Domain Admin; Schema Admins should be empty outside schema changes.

exchange.summary: LDAP search base=DC=scaffold,DC=htb scope=sub filter=(objectClass=*) attrs=[objectClass,cn,sAMAccountName,… +49]
273 entries returned

findings.impact: Members of these groups (Backup Operators, Server Operators, Print Operators, Account Operators, DnsAdmins, etc.) can escalate to Domain Admin via well-documented paths (SeBackupPrivilege dumps SAM, DnsAdmin ServerLevelPluginDll, etc.). Any account here should be treated as Tier-0.
findings.remediation: Empty these groups; use just-in-time membership for the rare legitimate operation.

findings.title: Weak domain password policy
findings.detail: The default domain password policy allows weak or long-lived credentials, easing brute-force and spray attacks.

exchange.summary: LDAP search base=DC=scaffold,DC=htb scope=sub filter=(objectClass=*) attrs=[objectClass,cn,sAMAccountName,… +49]
273 entries returned

findings.impact: Short minimum length + low complexity means accounts are crackable in hours from a single Kerberoast or AS-REP capture, and password-spray attacks succeed against multiple accounts before lockout fires.
findings.remediation: Enforce length >= 14, complexity on, a lockout threshold, and finite maximum password age.

findings.title: Privileged accounts are delegatable (missing 'sensitive, cannot be delegated')
findings.detail: The account's TGT can be delegated. An unconstrained-delegation host that the account authenticates to caches its TGT; a constrained/RBCD path can impersonate it.

exchange.summary: LDAP search base=DC=scaffold,DC=htb scope=sub filter=(objectClass=*) attrs=[objectClass,cn,sAMAccountName,… +49]
273 entries returned

findings.impact: Attacker coerces the admin to authenticate to a delegation-enabled host, captures the TGT, and replays it — Tier-0 access without the password.
findings.remediation: Set 'account is sensitive and cannot be delegated' (UAC NOT_DELEGATED) on Tier-0 accounts, or add them to Protected Users.

findings.title: 1 privileged accounts with non-expiring passwords
findings.detail: A privileged account with DONT_EXPIRE_PASSWORD keeps the same credential indefinitely — ideal for offline cracking, reuse, and breach persistence.

exchange.summary: LDAP search base=DC=scaffold,DC=htb scope=sub filter=(objectClass=*) attrs=[objectClass,cn,sAMAccountName,… +49]
273 entries returned

findings.impact: The password never rotates, so once cracked or captured (Kerberoast, NTDS dump, historical breach) it remains valid indefinitely. Privileged accounts are the highest-value targets; DONT_EXPIRE_PASSWORD on any is a persistence gift.
findings.remediation: Remove DONT_EXPIRE_PASSWORD from privileged accounts; migrate service accounts to gMSA.

findings.title: 1 disabled accounts still stamped privileged (adminCount=1)
findings.detail: A disabled but adminCount=1 account keeps its AdminSDHolder-protected ACL; anyone who can re-enable it (or its password) gains a Tier-0 identity.

exchange.summary: LDAP search base=DC=scaffold,DC=htb scope=sub filter=(objectClass=*) attrs=[objectClass,cn,sAMAccountName,… +49]
273 entries returned

findings.impact: adminCount=1 sticks even after the account is disabled: it keeps its AdminSDHolder-stamped ACLs and can be re-enabled without triggering a permission review. Re-enablement gives instant tier-0 access.
findings.remediation: Remove stale privileged accounts, or clear adminCount and re-baseline the ACL after removing them from protected groups.

findings.title: ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota = 10 (any user can join computers)
findings.detail: A non-zero quota lets any authenticated user create computer accounts — a prerequisite for RBCD and noPac (CVE-2021-42278/87) style attacks.

evidence.value: 10 (>0 ⇒ any authenticated user may join computers)

exchange.summary: LDAP search base=DC=scaffold,DC=htb scope=sub filter=(objectClass=*) attrs=[objectClass,cn,sAMAccountName,… +49]
273 entries returned

findings.impact: Any authenticated user can create up to that many computer objects, then abuse RBCD (msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity) via the newly-created machine account to impersonate any user against any service the machine controls, including Tier-0.
findings.remediation: Set ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota to 0 and delegate computer-join to a dedicated group.

findings.title: Service accounts negotiate RC4 Kerberos encryption
findings.detail: RC4 (etype 23) TGS tickets crack far faster than AES; missing msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes falls back to RC4.

exchange.summary: LDAP search base=DC=scaffold,DC=htb scope=sub filter=(objectClass=*) attrs=[objectClass,cn,sAMAccountName,… +49]
273 entries returned

findings.impact: TGS tickets for these accounts are encrypted with RC4-HMAC (MD4 of NT hash). Kerberoasting cracks them ~10x faster than AES-encrypted tickets, and unpatched RC4 downgrade lets an attacker force RC4 for any account.
findings.remediation: Set msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes to AES128+AES256 (0x18) on service accounts and DCs.

findings.title: Protected Users group is empty
findings.detail: Privileged accounts are not placed in Protected Users, so they remain exposed to credential theft (no RC4, no delegation, forced short TGT lifetime).

evidence.value: Domain Admins member count = 1 (Tier-0 accounts exist to protect)

exchange.summary: LDAP search base=DC=scaffold,DC=htb scope=sub filter=(objectClass=*) attrs=[objectClass,cn,sAMAccountName,… +49]
273 entries returned

findings.impact: Protected Users hardens membership against most credential-theft (no RC4 TGT, no unconstrained delegation, no NTLM). Empty = Tier-0 accounts remain vulnerable to Kerberoasting, PtH, and delegation abuse.
findings.remediation: Add Tier-0 accounts to Protected Users after validating compatibility.

findings.title: Built-in Administrator (RID 500) is in active use
findings.detail: The built-in Administrator should be a sealed break-glass account; routine use means a shared credential with no individual attribution and full Tier-0 rights.

exchange.summary: LDAP search base=DC=scaffold,DC=htb scope=sub filter=(objectClass=*) attrs=[objectClass,cn,sAMAccountName,… +49]
273 entries returned

findings.impact: The built-in Administrator is exempt from lockout policy and often has DONT_EXPIRE_PASSWORD. Active use means the credential is being shared or captured on hosts: any LSASS dump captures it with tier-0 rights.
findings.remediation: Reserve RID 500 for break-glass, use named admin accounts, and enable auditing/alerting on its logons.

composite_chains.title: Coercion + ADCS ESC8
composite_chains.impact: relay coerced DC NTLM to the CA's HTTP web-enrollment → DA machine cert → PKINIT for the DC TGT → DCSync.

composite_chains.title: ESC1 template enrollable by any user
composite_chains.impact: enroll a cert with SAN = arbitrary UPN → PKINIT for that user's TGT (typically DA).

composite_chains.title: MAQ > 0 + ADCS ESC8
composite_chains.impact: create rogue machine (MAQ let-through) → coerce it → relay its NTLM to CA web-enrollment → DA cert → PKINIT.

composite_chains.title: DCSync path + writable Shadow Credentials
composite_chains.impact: plant KeyCredentialLink on the DCSync-capable principal → PKINIT for its TGT → DCSync the whole domain.

coverage.title: Accounts do not require Kerberos pre-authentication
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Attackers can request an AS-REP for the account and offline-crack the encrypted timestamp. No credentials required to enumerate targets or run the attack.
coverage.remediation: Set DONT_REQ_PREAUTH=false on every account. If an app truly needs it, isolate the account and monitor Event ID 4768 with pre-auth type not equal to 2.

coverage.title: Privileged accounts are Kerberoastable (SPN + adminCount=1)
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Any authenticated user can request a service ticket for the admin's SPN and offline-crack the account password with hashcat mode 13100/19700. Direct path to DA.
coverage.remediation: Remove SPNs from privileged accounts. If an SPN is required, use a gMSA. Ensure passwords are ≥25 random chars.

coverage.title: Unconstrained delegation on non-DC principals
coverage.hypothetical_impact: If any account or service ticket is coerced to the target host, its TGT is cached and reusable for impersonation (Printer Bug / PetitPotam → TGT harvest → DA).
coverage.remediation: Set TRUSTED_FOR_DELEGATION=false on every non-DC. Migrate to constrained or RBCD with a specific service scope.

coverage.title: Direct control path to Tier-0 detected
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Any compromised principal in the listed path can write the ACL, gain DCSync/GenericAll on Tier-0, extract the krbtgt hash, and forge a golden ticket. Cost=1 means one dangerous action away, not one hop of pivoting.
coverage.remediation: Review the listed principals and remove unexpected ACEs (WriteDacl/GenericAll/Replication rights); re-apply the AdminSDHolder template where appropriate.

coverage.title: Shadow Credentials path to Tier-0 detected
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Attacker writes msDS-KeyCredentialLink on the Tier-0 target, then PKINITs with the freshly-generated cert to obtain a TGT as that principal. Full impersonation of a Domain Admin without ever learning their password.
coverage.remediation: Remove unexpected WriteProperty on msDS-KeyCredentialLink and audit AdminSDHolder inheritance on privileged accounts.

coverage.title: Populated sensitive / Tier-0-equivalent groups
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Members of these groups (Backup Operators, Server Operators, Print Operators, Account Operators, DnsAdmins, etc.) can escalate to Domain Admin via well-documented paths (SeBackupPrivilege dumps SAM, DnsAdmin ServerLevelPluginDll, etc.). Any account here should be treated as Tier-0.
coverage.remediation: Empty these groups; use just-in-time membership for the rare legitimate operation.

coverage.title: gMSA readable by broad principals
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Any listed principal can read the gMSA's managed password (msDS-ManagedPassword) via LDAPS and derive the NT hash for pass-the-hash.
coverage.remediation: Restrict PrincipalsAllowedToRetrieveManagedPassword to only the services that actually need the password — usually a dedicated computer or gMSA group.

coverage.title: SIDHistory populated on account
coverage.hypothetical_impact: SIDHistory grants effective rights from another domain. If SID Filtering is off between trusts, a forest-external attacker can inject Tier-0 SIDs to impersonate DA.
coverage.remediation: Clear SIDHistory after migration completes. Enable SID Filtering on all external trusts.

coverage.title: Resource-Based Constrained Delegation writeable
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Any principal with WriteProperty on msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity can point a target computer to authenticate to them, then S4U2Self+S4U2Proxy any user → impersonation.
coverage.remediation: Restrict who can write msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity. Audit computer objects for unexpected values.

coverage.title: Constrained delegation to service
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Account can act on behalf of any user to the target service via S4U2Proxy. Attacker who compromises the delegating account reaches the target as any user.
coverage.remediation: Reduce delegated SPN scope. Prefer Kerberos with A2D2 (protocol transition) only when strictly required.

coverage.title: Kerberoastable service accounts (user + SPN)
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Any authenticated user can request a service ticket for these SPNs and offline-crack the account password. Common footholds for weak service creds.
coverage.remediation: Migrate to gMSAs. If retention needed, enforce ≥25-char random passwords + AES256 only.

coverage.title: Privileged accounts are delegatable (missing 'sensitive, cannot be delegated')
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Attacker coerces the admin to authenticate to a delegation-enabled host, captures the TGT, and replays it — Tier-0 access without the password.
coverage.remediation: Set 'account is sensitive and cannot be delegated' (UAC NOT_DELEGATED) on Tier-0 accounts, or add them to Protected Users.

coverage.title: msDS-KeyCredentialLink set on Tier-0 account
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Anyone controlling that public key can authenticate via PKINIT as the Tier-0 identity — no password needed. Shadow Credentials attack payload.
coverage.remediation: Audit msDS-KeyCredentialLink on privileged accounts. Remove entries that don't match a legitimate WHfB device.

coverage.title: Non-admin user in Tier-0 group
coverage.hypothetical_impact: A non-privileged identity is a member of Domain Admins / Enterprise Admins → any compromise of that identity is instant DA.
coverage.remediation: Remove non-admin members. Use just-in-time / delegated groups for admin work rather than blanket Domain Admins membership.

coverage.title: Populated Key Admins / Enterprise Key Admins
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Key Admins can write msDS-KeyCredentialLink on any user → Shadow Credentials on any account, including Tier-0.
coverage.remediation: Empty Key Admins if not using Windows Hello for Business. Otherwise, restrict membership.

coverage.title: Administrator not in Protected Users
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Without Protected Users membership, the admin's NTLM hash is cached during logon and reversible (harvest → pass-the-hash → DA).
coverage.remediation: Add every Domain Admin to Protected Users. Requires DFL ≥ 2012R2.

coverage.title: Cross-forest principal in privileged group
coverage.hypothetical_impact: A SID from a foreign forest is present in a Tier-0 group. Any compromise in the foreign forest = DA in this one.
coverage.remediation: Review and remove foreign SIDs. Never grant cross-forest Tier-0 unless with SID Filtering and selective auth.

coverage.title: Computer account in a Tier-0 group
coverage.hypothetical_impact: A computer's machine account is Tier-0 → any code executing as SYSTEM on that box (unpatched RCE, local install-service) becomes DA.
coverage.remediation: Remove computer accounts from Domain Admins/Enterprise Admins. Use dedicated service accounts instead.

coverage.title: Constrained delegation to DC service
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Constrained delegation to cifs/host or ldap/dc lets the delegating account impersonate any user against the DC — often equivalent to DA.
coverage.remediation: Never delegate to DC services. Move sensitive delegations off the DC.

coverage.title: Non-default members of Group Policy Creator Owners
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Members can create GPOs and link them to OUs they own → GPO abuse for RCE on member machines via startup scripts or scheduled tasks.
coverage.remediation: Empty the group by default. Grant GPO creation on a per-OU basis via delegated permissions.

coverage.title: Computers without LAPS coverage
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Local admin passwords are static / reused across machines → one Local Admin compromise = lateral movement across the whole estate.
coverage.remediation: Install and configure LAPS (Windows LAPS since Server 2022). Enforce randomized rotation per machine.

coverage.title: Accounts with PASSWD_NOTREQD set
coverage.hypothetical_impact: The account can log on with an empty password. Anyone who guesses the samAccountName has instant access.
coverage.remediation: Clear the UAC bit UF_PASSWD_NOTREQD on every account. Set a strong password.

coverage.title: ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota = 10 (any user can join computers)
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Any authenticated user can create up to that many computer objects, then abuse RBCD (msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity) via the newly-created machine account to impersonate any user against any service the machine controls, including Tier-0.
coverage.remediation: Set ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota to 0 and delegate computer-join to a dedicated group.

coverage.title: krbtgt password has not been rotated in >180 days
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Old krbtgt hashes may have been previously exfiltrated by a former DA. Golden tickets forged with those hashes remain valid until krbtgt is rotated twice.
coverage.remediation: Rotate the krbtgt password TWICE (24h apart) to invalidate any pre-existing golden tickets. Automate rotation every 180 days.

coverage.title: Accounts store passwords with reversible encryption
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Passwords are decryptable from the DIT — anyone with SYSTEM on the DC recovers cleartext.
coverage.remediation: Clear the ENCRYPTED_TEXT_PWD_ALLOWED UAC bit on every user. Only legacy CHAP/DIGEST integrations legitimately need it.

coverage.title: Service accounts negotiate RC4 Kerberos encryption
coverage.hypothetical_impact: TGS tickets for these accounts are encrypted with RC4-HMAC (MD4 of NT hash). Kerberoasting cracks them ~10x faster than AES-encrypted tickets, and unpatched RC4 downgrade lets an attacker force RC4 for any account.
coverage.remediation: Set msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes to AES128+AES256 (0x18) on service accounts and DCs.

coverage.title: Delegated Managed Service Accounts present (badSuccessor exposure)
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Server 2025's dMSA feature lets an authorized user create a dMSA that inherits from ANY existing account, including Tier-0 (CVE-2024-BadSuccessor).
coverage.remediation: Audit dMSA creation rights. Restrict who can write msDS-DelegatedMSAState. Apply the Microsoft patch for BadSuccessor.

coverage.title: Weak domain password policy
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Short minimum length + low complexity means accounts are crackable in hours from a single Kerberoast or AS-REP capture, and password-spray attacks succeed against multiple accounts before lockout fires.
coverage.remediation: Enforce length >= 14, complexity on, a lockout threshold, and finite maximum password age.

coverage.title: dSHeuristics anonymous LDAP bind allowed
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Anonymous LDAP bind lets unauthenticated attackers enumerate users, groups, computers → target list for spray, ASREPRoast, and social engineering.
coverage.remediation: Clear position 7 in dSHeuristics (remove the '2' at that offset). Restart LDAP or wait for cache refresh.

coverage.title: Pre-Windows 2000 Compatible Access has Anonymous or Everyone
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Anonymous SID in this builtin group grants Read on User/Group objects → full domain enumeration without a bind.
coverage.remediation: Remove Anonymous Logon (S-1-5-7) and Everyone (S-1-1-0) from Pre-Windows 2000 Compatible Access.

coverage.title: Protected Users group is empty
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Protected Users hardens membership against most credential-theft (no RC4 TGT, no unconstrained delegation, no NTLM). Empty = Tier-0 accounts remain vulnerable to Kerberoasting, PtH, and delegation abuse.
coverage.remediation: Add Tier-0 accounts to Protected Users after validating compatibility.

coverage.title: Built-in Guest account is enabled
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Guest can browse SYSVOL, enumerate accounts, and mount lateral-movement primitives when Access Denied happens under authenticated context.
coverage.remediation: Disable the Guest account. Also disable Guest via GPO 'Accounts: Guest account status'.

coverage.title: User description contains apparent password
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Description field is world-readable. If a service password is stored there, any authenticated user (or Anonymous with weak posture) sees it.
coverage.remediation: Move creds to a secrets manager. Audit and blank the description on all users.

coverage.title: Fine-Grained Password Policy weaker than default
coverage.hypothetical_impact: FGPP applied to a group can weaken policy for those accounts below the default — used maliciously to lower Tier-0 barriers.
coverage.remediation: Review FGPPs targeting privileged groups. Set minimums equal to or stronger than default domain policy.

coverage.title: Cleartext secret in SYSVOL / GPP cpassword
coverage.hypothetical_impact: GPP cpassword uses a Microsoft-published AES key, so any file in SYSVOL Preferences with cpassword is decryptable by any authenticated user.
coverage.remediation: Remove all Groups.xml/Drives.xml/Scheduled Tasks with cpassword from SYSVOL. Rotate any credentials that were exposed.

coverage.title: Domain policy stores all passwords with reversible encryption
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Every password in the domain is decryptable from the DIT. Complete cleartext credential exposure to anyone with DCSync.
coverage.remediation: Clear DOMAIN_PASSWORD_STORE_CLEARTEXT (bit 16) from the domain pwdProperties attribute.

coverage.title: Multiple AD CS ESC misconfigurations
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Cert-based attacks (ESC1-16) yield authentication certificates for any account, including DA. See individual ESC findings for specifics.
coverage.remediation: Audit every published template. Remove ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT flag from unrestricted templates, tighten enrollment ACLs, require manager approval.

coverage.title: Cert template with weak key size (< 2048)
coverage.hypothetical_impact: 1024-bit RSA keys are feasible to factor. Certs issued from this template are forgeable given enough compute.
coverage.remediation: Set msPKI-Minimal-Key-Size ≥ 2048 on every template.

coverage.title: Trust does not enforce SID filtering
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Cross-forest attacker can inject SIDHistory entries with Tier-0 SIDs of the trusting forest → forest-wide DA via one compromise.
coverage.remediation: Enable SID filtering: netdom trust /... /Quarantine:Yes on external trusts, /EnableSIDHistory:No on forest trusts.

coverage.title: Trust does not enforce selective authentication
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Users from the trusted forest can authenticate to any resource in the trusting forest by default — no allow-list.
coverage.remediation: Enable selective authentication on the trust. Grant Allowed-To-Authenticate per-computer to trusted forest users.

coverage.title: TGT delegation across forest trust enabled
coverage.hypothetical_impact: TGTs delegated cross-forest → account authenticating to compromised trusted-forest server has its TGT stolen → impersonate DA.
coverage.remediation: Disable TGT delegation on the trust: netdom trust /... /EnableTgtDelegation:No.

coverage.title: Trust uses RC4 encryption
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Trust ticket RC4 is offline-crackable. Cross-forest attacker can forge inter-realm tickets after breaking the RC4 trust key.
coverage.remediation: Set trust to AES-only. Update trustAuthOutgoing/Incoming with AES256 keys via netdom trust /... /Kerberos.

coverage.title: External trust configured as transitive
coverage.hypothetical_impact: External trust transitivity extends the trust chain — Tier-0 in trusted domain reaches this one indirectly through intermediate forests.
coverage.remediation: External trusts should be non-transitive. If transitivity needed, upgrade to a forest trust with proper SID filtering.

coverage.title: Inactive user accounts (no logon in >180 days)
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Unmonitored account → password compromise stays undetected. Also becomes credential-theft target during audit dumps.
coverage.remediation: Disable accounts inactive > 90 days. Move disabled accounts to a dedicated OU for later cleanup.

coverage.title: Unsupported / end-of-life operating systems in the domain
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Unpatched OS = known RCE. Any authenticated user might exploit → SYSTEM on the domain member → path to DA.
coverage.remediation: Retire EOL systems. Isolate on segmented VLAN and monitor closely if retirement is delayed.

coverage.title: User account passwords not rotated in >2 years
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Ancient passwords are likely reused elsewhere and appear in credential-leak dumps. Trivial online / offline attack.
coverage.remediation: Enforce password expiration ≤ 365 days. Use FGPP to enforce shorter for privileged accounts.

coverage.title: Stale computers (no logon in >180 days)
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Computer accounts still trust and can be re-attached. If attacker owns the computer, its stored TGT and machine key remain valid.
coverage.remediation: Disable and eventually delete stale computer accounts. Auto-cleanup with `dsquery computer -inactive`.

coverage.title: Machine account password not rotated in >90 days
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Old machine password → hash still valid → SILVER TICKET remains usable. NRPC secure channel weak / vulnerable to Zerologon replay.
coverage.remediation: Ensure Machine Account Password Age GPO is set (30 days default). Investigate why rotation stopped for the flagged host.

coverage.title: LAPS password expired but not rotated
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Expired ms-Mcs-AdmPwdExpirationTime → LAPS agent hasn't rotated → password may be leaked already and never invalidated.
coverage.remediation: Investigate why the LAPS agent isn't rotating (offline machine? service broken?). Force rotation via Reset-AdmPwdPassword.

coverage.title: Duplicate SPN on two accounts
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Kerberos rejects service tickets for duplicated SPNs. Also, an attacker who owns one account can inject SPN collisions to hijack service auth.
coverage.remediation: Remove the duplicate SPN. Use `setspn -X` to enumerate collisions.

coverage.title: 1 privileged accounts with non-expiring passwords
coverage.hypothetical_impact: The password never rotates, so once cracked or captured (Kerberoast, NTDS dump, historical breach) it remains valid indefinitely. Privileged accounts are the highest-value targets; DONT_EXPIRE_PASSWORD on any is a persistence gift.
coverage.remediation: Remove DONT_EXPIRE_PASSWORD from privileged accounts; migrate service accounts to gMSA.

coverage.title: Accounts restricted to DES Kerberos keys
coverage.hypothetical_impact: DES tickets are trivially crackable (56-bit key). Any Kerberoast against these accounts recovers the password within seconds.
coverage.remediation: Clear USE_DES_KEY_ONLY UAC bit. Set msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes to 0x18 (AES128+256).

coverage.title: Domain / forest functional level obsolete
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Below 2012R2, Protected Users and Authentication Policies don't work; below 2008, essential Kerberos features (AES) are unavailable.
coverage.remediation: Raise DFL/FFL to the level supported by your oldest DC. Retire DCs on unsupported OSes.

coverage.title: 1 disabled accounts still stamped privileged (adminCount=1)
coverage.hypothetical_impact: adminCount=1 sticks even after the account is disabled: it keeps its AdminSDHolder-stamped ACLs and can be re-enabled without triggering a permission review. Re-enablement gives instant tier-0 access.
coverage.remediation: Remove stale privileged accounts, or clear adminCount and re-baseline the ACL after removing them from protected groups.

coverage.title: Accounts that have never logged on
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Unused account = unmonitored. If attacker sets a password on it (write ACE) or resurrects it, no alert fires.
coverage.remediation: Disable accounts that have never logged on and are older than 30 days. Delete if unclaimed after a review.

coverage.title: Account privileged via primaryGroupID (hidden membership)
coverage.hypothetical_impact: The account is effectively a Domain Admin via primaryGroupID = 512 without appearing in the group's member list — bypasses many audit tools.
coverage.remediation: Restore primaryGroupID to Domain Users (513). Only special service accounts (like krbtgt) should use non-default primaryGroupID.

coverage.title: Privileged accounts have not logged on in >90 days
coverage.hypothetical_impact: Dormant admin accounts are prime harvesting targets — nobody monitors their activity, so credential theft goes unnoticed longer.
coverage.remediation: Disable admin accounts that haven't logged on in 90 days. Rotate their passwords first, then set them disabled.

coverage.title: Built-in Administrator (RID 500) is in active use
coverage.hypothetical_impact: The built-in Administrator is exempt from lockout policy and often has DONT_EXPIRE_PASSWORD. Active use means the credential is being shared or captured on hosts: any LSASS dump captures it with tier-0 rights.
coverage.remediation: Reserve RID 500 for break-glass, use named admin accounts, and enable auditing/alerting on its logons.
